column2: What effector distinguishes each of the four classical hypersensitivity types?
column3: Type I is immediate and IgE-mediated, type II uses antibodies against cells, matrix or receptors, type III uses soluble immune complexes, and type IV is T-cell mediated.

column2: Why is intramuscular adrenaline, not an antihistamine, first-line for anaphylaxis?

column2: Why do broad allergy panels risk harm, and what should diagnosis rest on instead?

column2: After allogeneic haematopoietic transplantation, why is suppressing donor T cells a trade-off?
